construction_markdown:
No new leaderboard candidate is advanced; the active proved `k=1040` construction dominates the following exact subfield-subcode witness.

Let `F=F_2[alpha]/(alpha^30+alpha+1)`, using the accepted irreducibility certificate in `algebraic-04`. Put

`q=2^30`, `Q=q-1`, `B=q-535822336=537919488=2^29+2^20`.

For a positive integer `u`, write `[u]_Q` for its representative in `{1,...,Q}` modulo `Q`. Use the nine doubling-orbit representatives

`E={1,513,1025,2049,4097,8193,16385,32769,1049601}`

`={1,1+2^9,...,1+2^15,1+2^10+2^20}`.

Their orbit sizes under `e -> [2e]_Q` are respectively

`30,30,30,30,30,30,30,15,10`.

For an orbit representative `e` of size `r`, let `F_(2^r)={beta in F: beta^(2^r)=beta}`. Choose its canonical binary basis by reduced row echelon reduction of the linear map `beta -> beta^(2^r)+beta` in the fixed polynomial basis. For every basis element `beta`, define

`f_(e,beta)(X)=sum_(j=0)^(r-1) beta^(2^j) X^([2^j e]_Q)`.

The generator rows are the evaluations of `1` and all these polynomials on every `x in F`, with both rows and coordinates in the specified increasing polynomial-basis order. There are

`1+7*30+15+10=236`

rows. This is exactly the full-field binary subfield subcode

`ev_F(F[X]_(degree<=B)) intersect F_2^q`.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For algebraic positions 4, 5, and 6: if `S(a,t)=ev_(F_(2^a))(F_(2^a)[X]_(<=t)) intersect F_2^(2^a)`, then `dim S(a,t)=1+sum |O|`, where the sum runs over doubling orbits modulo `2^a-1` contained wholly in `{1,...,t}`. At `a=30` and `t=2^29+2^20`, the permitted orbit sizes are `30,30,30,30,30,30,30,15,10`, so the exact dimension is `236`. The coefficient-orbit proof is elementary from `f^2=f mod (X^(2^a)-X)`.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For the construction architect and bottleneck breaker: the full-field ordinary-RS subfield-subcode route cannot supply the conditional `[16384,17,8188]_2` inner code. Before degree `8256` its dimension is at most `15`. At degree `8256` it acquires the seven-dimensional norm-trace orbit, but already contains `1+Tr_(128/2)(x^129)` of weight `8128`. Thus every full subfield subcode of dimension at least `17` has distance at most `8128`.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For the architecture and parameter positions: concatenate a full-field RS subfield subcode of length `2^a` with an ordinary RS outer code of length `2^(30-a)`, and certify distance by the two RS root bounds. Exact orbit counting gives the dimension ceilings `1040,561,306,252,195,153,128` for `a=15,...,21`; all `a>=22` give at most `236`, while `a<=14` fails the outer-alphabet-size condition. Equality `1040` occurs only at `a=15`, the affine `RM(1,15)` inner code, and outer dimension `65`.

distance_audit: Every row polynomial satisfies `f^2=f modulo X^q-X`; consequently every evaluated entry lies in `F_2`.
All listed exponent orbits lie at or below `B=537919488`. Every binary combination is represented by a polynomial of degree at most `B`.
Disjoint exponent supports and independent subfield coefficient bases show that a nonzero row combination is a nonzero polynomial.
A nonzero polynomial of degree at most `B<q` has at most `B` roots in `F`, hence its binary evaluation has weight at least `q-B=535822336`.
For the length-16384 obstruction, the norm map has fibers of size 129, giving signed sum `-128`, weight `8256`, and complementary weight `8128`.
The `k<=1040` concatenation statement is explicitly scoped to distance certified by the inherited inner root bound and ordinary outer-RS distance.
explicitness_audit: The field is the fixed accepted quotient by `T^30+T+1`; no irreducible-polynomial search or unspecified isomorphism is used.
All nine cyclotomic representatives and all orbit sizes are displayed symbolically.
The degree-15 and degree-10 subfield bases are computed deterministically as canonical nullspace bases of explicit 30-by-30 binary Frobenius matrices.
Rows, field elements, coordinates, exponent orbits, and basis vectors have fixed orders.
The complete 236-by-1073741824 matrix is emitted, not accessed through an oracle or finite lookup.
There is no random sampling, exhaustive witness selection, or conditional-expectation recursion.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Use the fixed polynomial basis of `F_2[T]/(T^30+T+1)`. Compute canonical bases of `ker(z -> z^(2^r)+z)` for `r=30,15,10`. Emit the constant row. Then, for each displayed orbit representative `e` and each canonical basis element `beta` of the corresponding subfield, enumerate all `x in F` and emit `sum_j beta^(2^j)x^([2^j e]_(2^30-1))`, which the proof shows is either 0 or 1.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: `O(236*n*(log n)^3+(log n)^4)` bit operations; at the fixed target this is `O(n)` with an explicitly bounded 236-row output.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: Let `m=30`. Canonical subfield bases require Gaussian elimination on `m`-dimensional binary maps, costing `O(m^4)`. For one matrix entry, compute `x^e` by at most `m` square-and-multiply stages, obtain the remaining at most `m-1` orbit powers by squaring, and form at most `m` coefficient products. Schoolbook arithmetic modulo the fixed degree-`m` polynomial costs `O(m^2)` bits per field operation, hence `O(m^3)` per emitted entry. There are exactly `236n` entries.

proof_markdown:
Let `E_a=F_(2^a)` and

`S(a,t)=ev_(E_a)({f in E_a[X]: deg f<=t}) intersect F_2^(2^a)`.

### 1. Cyclotomic-orbit decomposition

Every function on `E_a` has a unique polynomial representative of degree below `2^a`. If such an `f` is binary-valued, then

`f(X)^2 = f(X) modulo X^(2^a)-X`.

For positive exponents, squaring sends `e` to `[2e]_(2^a-1)`. Hence its coefficients satisfy

`c_[2e]=c_e^2`.

The nonzero support is therefore a union of complete doubling orbits contained in `{1,...,t}`. On an orbit of size `r`, all coefficients are determined by one `beta` satisfying `beta^(2^r)=beta`; this contributes exactly `r` binary dimensions. The constant coefficient contributes one dimension. Conversely, the displayed orbit polynomial for every such `beta` is fixed by squaring and is binary-valued. Therefore

`dim S(a,t)=1+sum_(O subset {1,...,t}) |O|`. (1)

Multiplication by two modulo `2^a-1` is cyclic rotation of the `a`-bit representation of an exponent.

### 2. Exact target count

For `a=30`, the cutoff is `B=2^29+2^20`. Suppose a cyclic bit word has all rotations at most `B`. If it has two ones, rotating either one to position 29 shows that both cyclic gaps between them must be at least 9. Thus, up to rotation, their separation is `s=9,...,15`.

If the word has at least three ones, after rotating one to position 29 the nearest lower one cannot be at distance 9: its contribution would already be `2^20`, and another positive term would exceed `B`. Hence every cyclic gap is at least 10. Their sum is 30, so the only possibility is three gaps `10,10,10`.

Consequently the nonconstant admissible orbits are: one weight-one orbit of size 30; six size-30 weight-two orbits for separations 9 through 14; one size-15 orbit for separation 15; and the size-10 three-one orbit. Equation (1) gives `1+30+180+15+10=236`.

Every nonzero polynomial in this subfield subcode has degree at most `B`, hence at most `B` roots. Its binary evaluation has weight at least

`2^30-B=535822336`.

Disjoint orbit supports also prove that the 236 displayed rows are independent.

### 3. The length-16384 gateway obstruction

For `a=14`, every cyclic word with at least two ones has a cyclic gap at most 7. Rotating the adjacent one to position 13 gives an exponent at least

`2^13+2^6=8256`.

Thus `dim S(14,t)<=15` for `t<=8255`. At `t=8256`, the new size-seven orbit is represented by `129=1+2^7`. It contains

`h(x)=Tr_(F_128/F_2)(x^129)`.

For nonzero `x`, `x^129` is the norm from `F_(2^14)` to `F_(2^7)`, and every nonzero norm value has 129 preimages. Therefore

`sum_x (-1)^h(x)=1+129 sum_(y in F_128^*) (-1)^Tr(y)=1-129=-128`.

Hence `wt(h)=8256` and `wt(1+h)=8128`. Every later full subfield subcode contains this word. It follows that no `S(14,t)` has both dimension at least 17 and minimum distance at least 8188.

### 4. Concatenation ceiling

Use `S(a,t)` as an inner code of length `L=2^a` and dimension `r`, and an ordinary `[N,K,N-K+1]_(2^r)` RS outer code with `N=2^(30-a)`. Product certification requires

`(L-t)(N-K+1)>=D`.

Because `N-K+1<=N`, necessarily

`t<=B_a=floor(513*2^a/1024)`.

For `a>=10`, `B_a=2^(a-1)+2^(a-10)`. The same cyclic-gap argument shows that for `a<=17`, `r<=a+1`; for `a=18,19,20,21`, respectively, `r<=28,39,51,64`; and for every `22<=a<=30`, `r<=236`. For `a<=14`, the outer feasibility condition `N<=2^r` fails.

If `t<2^(a-1)`, then `r=1`, which is infeasible except for `a>=29` and yields dimension at most two. Otherwise `L-t<=L/2`, so

`N-K+1 >= ceil(511N/512)`,

and therefore

`K<=floor(N/512)+1`.

For `a=15,...,21`, multiplying by the preceding bounds on `r` gives

`1040,561,306,252,195,153,128`.

For `a>=22`, `K<=1` and `rK<=236`. Thus the scoped family has maximum 1040. Equality forces `a=15`, `t=2^14`, `r=16`, and `K=65`: precisely the known `RM(1,15)`-inner RS construction.

proof_steps.proof: No nonlinear orbit appears below degree 8256. The first orbit is the norm-trace orbit, and its constant translate has weight 8128 by the exact 129-to-one norm-fiber calculation.

proof_steps.proof: The product inequality forces `t<=B_a`; orbit counts bound the inner dimension, outer alphabet feasibility removes `a<=14`, and `K<=floor(N/512)+1` gives the displayed finite table.

proof_steps.proof: All rows are fixed orbit polynomials over canonical Frobenius-kernel bases and are evaluated in fixed order. The nested loops emit `236n` entries in `O(n(log n)^3)` bit operations.

theorem_statement: For the full-field ordinary Reed–Solomon binary subfield subcode `S(a,t)=ev_(F_(2^a))(F_(2^a)[X]_(<=t)) intersect F_2^(2^a)`, the dimension equals one plus the total sizes of the doubling orbits modulo `2^a-1` contained below `t`. At the immutable target cutoff `a=30`, `t=537919488`, this gives an explicit `[2^30,236,>=535822336]_2` code. At `a=14`, no full `S(14,t)` has both dimension at least 17 and distance at least 8188. Moreover, every exact-length concatenation using such a full subfield subcode as inner code, an ordinary RS outer code, and the inherited root/product distance certificate has dimension at most 1040, with equality only at the already-known `RM(1,15)`-inner parameters.
title: Cyclotomic-orbit closure: k=236 direct cap and k=1040 concatenation ceiling
